data.description: A rare benign vascular tumor of the umbilical cord, usually arising near the fetal cord insertion and composed of proliferating blood vessels within edematous or myxoid Wharton's jelly.
symptoms_in_common: Well-circumscribed fetal/umbilical-cord-associated mass on prenatal MRI and ultrasound
Small lobulated gross mass measuring approximately 3 cm
Histology showing numerous vascular channels in a fibrous or myxoid stromal background
Immunohistochemical vascular-marker positivity in endothelial-lined channels
Prominent collagenous stroma on trichrome staining
symptoms_not_in_common: No maternal symptoms, fetal hydrops, growth restriction, anemia, or signs of high-output cardiac failure are provided

data.description: A benign mesenchymal tumor-like lesion of the umbilical cord characterized by myxoid Wharton's jelly, spindle cells, and variably prominent small blood vessels; it may overlap morphologically with cord hemangioma.
symptoms_in_common: Prenatally detected umbilical-cord-region mass
Lobulated pale-yellow to tan gross appearance
Abundant myxoid/fibrous stromal tissue
Small vascular spaces scattered through the lesion
Collagen-rich stromal component on special staining
symptoms_not_in_common: A strongly circumscribed vascular proliferation is more suggestive of hemangioma than a predominantly myxoid angiomyxoma
No description of marked diffuse myxoid degeneration or a large pseudocystic cord lesion is provided

data.diagnosis: Umbilical cord pseudocyst associated with edema of Wharton's jelly
data.description: A pseudocyst is a localized accumulation of fluid within degenerated or edematous Wharton's jelly rather than a true epithelial-lined cyst. It can appear as a cord mass on prenatal imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Mass involving the umbilical cord region on prenatal imaging
Possible edematous/myxoid Wharton's jelly in the lesion
Cord-associated lesion that may change appearance on serial imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The pathology demonstrates vascular channels rather than a simple fluid-filled cavity
The gross lesion appears solid and lobulated rather than predominantly cystic
No true pseudocystic cavity is evident in the provided pathology images

data.description: A benign vascular tumor of the placenta composed of capillary-sized vascular channels embedded in fibrous stroma. Large lesions can cause fetal anemia, hydrops, polyhydramnios, or cardiac strain.
symptoms_in_common: Prenatally detected vascular-appearing mass
Lobulated gross lesion
Histologic proliferation of small vascular channels in fibrous stroma
Endothelial-marker-positive vascular spaces
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears associated with the umbilical cord rather than within placental parenchyma
No placental mass is specifically described
No fetal hydrops, polyhydramnios, anemia, or high-output cardiac failure is reported

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting tumor arising from adrenal medullary chromaffin cells; it is often a hypervascular adrenal mass and can show high signal on T2-weighted MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Hypervascular solid-appearing suprarenal/adrenal-region mass on Doppler ultrasound
MRI appearance of a focal adrenal-region lesion with relatively high T2 signal
No clinical symptoms were provided
symptoms_not_in_common: No episodic headache reported
No palpitations reported
No diaphoresis reported
No hypertension reported
No tremor or anxiety symptoms reported

data.description: A common benign tumor of the adrenal cortex, frequently discovered incidentally. Most are nonfunctioning, although some produce cortisol or aldosterone.
symptoms_in_common: Focal adrenal-region mass on ultrasound and MRI
Absence of provided systemic symptoms is compatible with an incidental nonfunctioning adenoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked internal vascularity is less typical for a lipid-rich adrenal adenoma
Relatively high T2 signal is less typical than the usually low-to-intermediate T2 signal of an adenoma
No features of cortisol excess such as weight gain, proximal weakness, bruising, or diabetes were reported
No features of hyperaldosteronism such as hypertension or hypokalemia were reported

data.description: Secondary malignant involvement of the adrenal gland, most commonly from lung cancer, melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, breast cancer, or gastrointestinal malignancy. Metastases are often indeterminate adrenal masses on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Solid adrenal-region lesion on multiple imaging modalities
Potentially heterogeneous appearance and vascularity
No clinical symptoms were provided
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy reported
No weight loss reported
No fatigue or constitutional symptoms reported
No bilateral adrenal involvement described
No symptoms of adrenal insufficiency reported

data.description: A rare malignant tumor of the adrenal cortex that may be hormonally active and usually presents as a large heterogeneous adrenal mass with necrosis, hemorrhage, or invasion when advanced.
symptoms_in_common: Solid adrenal-region mass with internal vascularity
Potentially heterogeneous MRI appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: No large invasive mass or metastatic disease is described
No abdominal pain or palpable mass reported
No virilization, feminization, or Cushing syndrome symptoms reported
No unexplained weight loss reported
No clinical symptoms were provided

data.description: A primary malignant tumor of liver cells, commonly presenting as a dominant hepatic mass with satellite nodules or additional intrahepatic tumors.
symptoms_in_common: Large heterogeneous liver mass
Additional smaller hepatic lesion suggesting satellite or multifocal disease
Appearance of a hypervascular hepatic neoplasm on contrast CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, liver disease history, cirrhosis, hepatitis status, or laboratory results were provided

data.description: A variant of hepatocellular carcinoma that often occurs in younger patients without cirrhosis and may appear as a large solitary heterogeneous liver mass, sometimes with satellite lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Large dominant hepatic mass
Heterogeneous internal appearance of the lesion
Possible additional intrahepatic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: A central scar or calcification is not clearly demonstrated
Patient age and absence of underlying cirrhosis are not provided
No clinical symptoms or laboratory findings were provided

data.description: A primary cancer of the intrahepatic bile ducts that can form a large liver mass and may produce satellite nodules or multifocal liver involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Large hepatic mass
Possible satellite lesion in another liver segment
Heterogeneous tumor appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Biliary ductal dilatation is not evident in the provided image
Jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, and cholestatic laboratory abnormalities were not provided

data.description: Secondary malignant tumors in the liver originating from a cancer elsewhere in the body; they may present as multiple lesions, including a dominant large metastasis.
symptoms_in_common: More than one focal liver lesion
Large heterogeneous hepatic lesion
Smaller additional hepatic lesion compatible with multifocal tumor involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary extrahepatic malignancy is provided
No systemic symptoms such as weight loss, fatigue, or known cancer history are provided

data.description: A benign hepatocellular tumor that can become large and heterogeneous because of fat, necrosis, or hemorrhage; multiple adenomas can occur in hepatic adenomatosis.
symptoms_in_common: Large focal liver mass
Potentially heterogeneous internal appearance
Possible additional liver lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging appearance may be more concerning for malignant multifocal disease than for a benign adenoma
Risk factors such as oral contraceptive use, anabolic steroid exposure, obesity, or glycogen storage disease are not provided
No abdominal pain or hemorrhagic symptoms are provided

data.description: A hereditary optic neuropathy causing slowly progressive bilateral optic nerve degeneration, temporal optic disc pallor, and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic disc pallor/optic atrophy
Bilateral reduction in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness on OCT
Symmetric involvement of both eyes
No obvious brain or spinal cord lesion on the provided MRI images
symptoms_not_in_common: No visual-acuity loss, color-vision deficit, central scotoma, hearing loss, or family history is provided

data.description: A mitochondrial inherited optic neuropathy that typically produces subacute painless central visual loss followed by bilateral optic atrophy; early fundus findings may include peripapillary telangiectatic vessels and later retinal nerve fiber layer loss.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic nerve atrophy
Marked bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Prominent/tortuous peripapillary retinal vessels may be compatible with LHON
Brain MRI may be normal
symptoms_not_in_common: No subacute central visual loss is described
No central scotoma or dyschromatopsia is provided
No mitochondrial family history is provided
No information about typical demographic risk factors, such as young adult male sex, is provided

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis-associated optic neuritis with residual optic atrophy
data.description: Inflammatory demyelination of the optic nerve can cause optic neuritis and, after prior episodes, residual optic disc pallor and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning. Multiple sclerosis may also cause brain and spinal cord demyelinating lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Optic atrophy can follow prior optic neuritis
Retinal nerve fiber layer thinning is consistent with prior optic nerve inflammation
Bilateral involvement can occur, particularly after recurrent episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of painful acute visual loss is provided
No neurologic relapses, sensory symptoms, weakness, or coordination symptoms are provided
The displayed brain MRI does not show clear typical demyelinating plaques
The displayed spinal MRI does not show an obvious demyelinating cord lesion

data.diagnosis: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) or MOG-antibody-associated optic neuritis
data.description: Autoimmune inflammatory disorders that can cause severe, often bilateral optic neuritis with subsequent optic atrophy and retinal nerve fiber layer loss; NMOSD may additionally produce longitudinally extensive myelitis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic nerve damage/optic atrophy
Substantial bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Brain MRI can be normal or nonspecific in some affected patients
symptoms_not_in_common: No episode of acute severe optic neuritis is described
No eye pain or visual-loss history is provided
No transverse myelitis symptoms, including limb weakness, sensory level, or bladder dysfunction, are provided

data.description: A rare autosomal-recessive iron-metabolism disorder caused by ceruloplasmin deficiency, leading to iron deposition in the brain, liver, pancreas, and retina.

Potential liver involvement

data.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by abnormal iron accumulation, particularly in the globus pallidus and substantia nigra, often causing dystonia, parkinsonism, and cognitive decline.
symptoms_in_common: Deep basal ganglia signal abnormalities
Imaging concern for abnormal metal deposition
symptoms_not_in_common: Pathogenic ATP7B mutation is not a typical cause of NBIA
Kayser-Fleischer-type corneal ring is not characteristic of NBIA
Liver involvement is not typical of most NBIA disorders
No dystonia, parkinsonism, spasticity, or cognitive decline was reported

data.description: Manganese accumulation can occur in chronic liver dysfunction or portosystemic shunting and may produce bilateral basal ganglia, especially globus pallidus, T1 hyperintensity with neurologic symptoms resembling parkinsonism.
symptoms_in_common: T1 hyperintensity in deep basal ganglia compatible with metal deposition
Possible hepatic pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: ATP7B pathogenic mutation strongly favors Wilson disease instead
Kayser-Fleischer-type corneal ring is not typical of manganese deposition
T2, DWI, and FLAIR basal ganglia degenerative signal changes are less characteristic than isolated pallidal T1 hyperintensity
No chronic liver failure, portosystemic shunt, or parkinsonian symptoms were reported

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated skin disease causing well-demarcated red plaques, often with silvery scale, commonly affecting extensor surfaces such as the elbows and knees.
symptoms_in_common: Red inflammatory plaques on the extensor surfaces of both elbows
Bilateral, relatively symmetric involvement
Possible mild scaling or thickened skin in the involved areas
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly visible thick silvery-white scale
No reported scalp, knee, nail, or other typical psoriasis involvement
No reported itching, pain, or chronic recurrent course

data.description: A chronic intensely itchy blistering skin disorder associated with gluten sensitivity/celiac disease, typically producing grouped papules, vesicles, and excoriations on extensor surfaces.
symptoms_in_common: Distribution over the elbows/extensor surfaces
Multiple small red papules or excoriated-looking lesions
Bilateral involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible grouped vesicles or blisters
No reported severe itching or burning
No reported gastrointestinal symptoms, gluten sensitivity, or celiac disease

data.description: Firm subcutaneous nodules that commonly occur over pressure points, especially the elbows, in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and occasionally other inflammatory conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent nodular swelling around the elbow/olecranon region
Location over an extensor pressure point
Possible bilateral elbow involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesions appear red and plaque-like rather than clearly firm skin-colored subcutaneous nodules
No reported rheumatoid arthritis, joint pain, morning stiffness, or hand joint swelling
No reported systemic inflammatory symptoms

data.description: Deposits of monosodium urate crystals in soft tissues due to longstanding hyperuricemia, often occurring around elbows, ears, fingers, toes, and joints.
symptoms_in_common: Nodular prominence near the elbow
Location around a joint and pressure area
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible chalky-white or yellow-white deposits
No reported recurrent acute attacks of severe joint pain, swelling, or redness
No reported history of hyperuricemia or gout

data.description: Inflammation of the skin caused by exposure to an allergen or irritant, producing redness, papules, swelling, scaling, and sometimes itching or blistering.
symptoms_in_common: Red patches and papules on the skin
Possible inflammation and swelling around the involved areas
Lesions may occur where skin contacts clothing, surfaces, topical products, or occupational exposures
symptoms_not_in_common: The bilateral extensor-elbow pattern is more suggestive of certain inflammatory dermatoses than a simple contact reaction
No reported new exposure, topical product, chemical, clothing, or adhesive trigger
No reported itching, burning, or sharply demarcated exposure pattern

data.description: Rapidly progressive cellulitis of the submandibular, sublingual, and submental spaces, often arising from an odontogenic infection and capable of causing airway obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Marked swelling of the tongue and floor of the mouth
Apparent narrowing of the upper airway/oropharyngeal airway
Dental abnormality or dental hardware visible near the presumed potential source region
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, dental pain, neck tenderness, drooling, or systemic illness is provided in the case description

data.diagnosis: Angioedema involving the tongue and upper airway
data.description: Acute edema of submucosal tissues, commonly affecting the lips, tongue, floor of mouth, and larynx; it may be allergic, medication-related, or hereditary and can threaten the airway.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse marked tongue enlargement
Upper-airway soft-tissue swelling
Potential airway compromise requiring airway support
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of sudden allergic exposure, ACE-inhibitor use, urticaria, facial swelling, or recurrent episodes is provided
Dental-region findings may suggest an infectious source rather than isolated angioedema

data.description: A localized purulent infection within the tongue, sublingual space, or adjacent deep neck spaces that can produce swelling, pain, dysphagia, and airway narrowing.
symptoms_in_common: Marked enlargement of the tongue/floor-of-mouth soft tissues
Oropharyngeal airway narrowing
Possible association with odontogenic infection
symptoms_not_in_common: A discrete rim-enhancing fluid collection is not clearly demonstrated on this single noncontrast sagittal image
No fever, focal tongue pain, dysphagia, or leukocytosis is provided

data.description: Bleeding into tongue tissues, often after trauma, seizure, anticoagulation, instrumentation, or dental procedures, causing rapid tongue enlargement and possible airway obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Pronounced tongue swelling
Potential upper-airway obstruction
Possible relevance of oral/dental instrumentation
symptoms_not_in_common: No trauma, anticoagulant use, seizure, recent procedure, bruising, or hyperdense blood collection is provided
The appearance may be more consistent with diffuse inflammatory edema than a focal hematoma

A usually benign pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that secretes insulin autonomously, causing recurrent fasting hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated endogenous insulin secretion.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoglycemia (glucose 2.4 mmol/L)
Inappropriately elevated insulin during hypoglycemia (574 pmol/L)
Elevated C-peptide indicating endogenous insulin production (3.214 nmol/L)
Relatively suppressed beta-hydroxybutyrate during hypoglycemia, consistent with insulin-mediated inhibition of ketone production

data.description: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin-secretagogue medications, such as sulfonylureas or meglitinides, which stimulate pancreatic insulin release and can mimic insulinoma laboratory findings.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoglycemia (glucose 2.4 mmol/L)
High insulin concentration during hypoglycemia
High C-peptide concentration due to stimulated endogenous insulin secretion
Low or inappropriately non-elevated beta-hydroxybutyrate due to insulin effect

data.description: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causing excessive endogenous insulin secretion, often producing postprandial hypoglycemia but sometimes fasting hypoglycemia as well.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia
Elevated insulin during hypoglycemia
Elevated C-peptide demonstrating endogenous insulin secretion
Suppressed ketone production relative to the severity of hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No information is provided about postprandial timing of hypoglycemic episodes, which is commonly reported in NIPHS

data.description: A rare autoimmune disorder in which insulin autoantibodies bind and later release insulin, causing spontaneous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia without exogenous insulin use.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia
Markedly elevated insulin concentration
C-peptide may be elevated or not fully suppressed because insulin secretion is endogenous
Reduced ketone production during insulin-mediated hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No insulin autoantibody result is provided
Insulin levels in insulin autoimmune syndrome are often much more extremely elevated than the reported value

data.description: A hypermobility disorder of the lower false ribs, usually ribs 8 to 10, caused by lax or disrupted interchondral attachments. A rib tip may move beneath or over an adjacent rib and irritate intercostal nerves.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance involving the lower false ribs, particularly the 8th and 9th ribs
Apparent close approximation or abnormal relative positioning of adjacent rib segments
symptoms_not_in_common: No pain, clicking, popping sensation, tenderness, or movement-provoked symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Congenital rib anomaly with bifid or fused rib
data.description: A developmental variation in which a rib may be partially split, unusually shaped, or connected to an adjacent rib. Such anomalies can be incidentally identified on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal-appearing configuration of the 7th through 9th ribs on ultrasound
Possible unusual relationship between adjacent ribs
symptoms_not_in_common: No congenital history or longstanding chest-wall asymmetry was provided
No respiratory symptoms or chest-wall discomfort were reported

data.diagnosis: Healed rib fracture with callus formation
data.description: A prior rib fracture can heal with cortical irregularity, angulation, or callus, altering the contour and spacing of adjacent ribs.
symptoms_in_common: Possible irregular contour or altered alignment of a lower rib on ultrasound
Involvement of ribs that are susceptible to trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of chest trauma was provided
No focal rib pain, bruising, swelling, or pain with breathing was reported

data.diagnosis: Chest-wall deformity due to rib crowding or focal costal cartilage deformity
data.description: A localized chest-wall structural deformity may alter rib spacing or produce prominence of one rib relative to neighboring ribs. It may be congenital, developmental, or post-traumatic.
symptoms_in_common: Altered apparent spacing and contour among the 7th, 8th, and 9th ribs
Localized lower chest-wall structural abnormality on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible chest-wall asymmetry or palpable lump was described
No pain, shortness of breath, or functional limitation was reported

data.description: A benign or secondary condition in which gas-filled cysts develop within the bowel wall, most often in the submucosa or subserosa of the colon.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple smooth, polypoid or grape-like submucosal colonic lesions on colonoscopy
Multiple intramural gas cysts seen on contrast radiography
Endoscopic ultrasound appearance of cystic gas-containing spaces within the bowel wall
Histology showing empty cystic spaces in the submucosa with surrounding inflammatory or foreign-body giant-cell reaction

data.description: A benign malformation or proliferation of lymphatic vessels that can produce multiple cystic, submucosal colonic lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple smooth submucosal polypoid lesions
Cyst-like lesions within the bowel wall
Possible incidental discovery during colonoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Intramural gas cysts on contrast radiography
Gas-related acoustic features on endoscopic ultrasound
Histologic empty spaces associated with a foreign-body giant-cell reaction typical of ruptured gas cysts

data.description: Benign fatty submucosal tumors of the colon that may appear as smooth, rounded protrusions into the lumen.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth rounded submucosal-appearing colonic protrusions on colonoscopy
May be asymptomatic or found incidentally
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous intramural gas-filled cysts on barium examination
Cystic gas spaces on endoscopic ultrasound
Histology showing empty spaces with giant-cell reaction rather than mature adipose tissue

data.description: A group of inherited or sporadic disorders characterized by numerous mucosal polyps in the colon, such as adenomatous or hamartomatous polyposis.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple polypoid lesions visualized in the colon
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions appear submucosal and cystic rather than true mucosal polyps
Intramural gas cysts on contrast radiography
Gas-containing spaces on endoscopic ultrasound
Histology consistent with pneumatosis and foreign-body giant-cell reaction rather than adenomatous or hamartomatous polyps

data.description: Peripheral blood/biochemistry: WBC 7,700/µL with marked eosinophilia (53.5%) and basophilia (4.0%); anemia (Hgb 8.6 g/dL, RBC 366 ×10^4/µL); platelets 25.5 ×10^4/µL. CRP elevated at 2.66 mg/dL. IgE 254 IU/mL and soluble IL-2 receptor 495 U/mL. ANA, Jo-1 antibody, RF, PR-ANCA, MPO-ANCA negative. Renal and liver function tests largely normal. Arterial blood gas showed alkalemia (pH 7.549) with low pCO2 (27.1 mmHg) and mildly low pO2 (68.2 mmHg). Viral markers for HBV, HCV, and HIV were negative.

data.diagnosis: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified (CEL-NOS)
data.description: A clonal myeloid neoplasm characterized by persistent hypereosinophilia, often with dysplastic eosinophil precursors, anemia, abnormal cytogenetics, and possible progression to acute leukemia.
symptoms_in_common: Marked absolute eosinophilia (WBC 7,700/µL with 53.5% eosinophils)
Eosinophilic myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands, and mature eosinophils on peripheral smear
Megaloblast-like/dysplastic hematopoietic cells and irregular hypersegmented neutrophils
Anemia (hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL)
Basophilia
Abnormal karyotype involving chromosomes 1 and 7
Mild elevation of inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild hypoxemia with respiratory alkalosis is not a defining feature
Elevated CRP is nonspecific rather than characteristic
Platelet count is preserved rather than clearly decreased or increased

data.diagnosis: Myelodysplastic syndrome with eosinophilia and der(1;7)/t(1;7) abnormality
data.description: A myelodysplastic neoplasm with ineffective hematopoiesis and dysplastic blood-cell morphology; abnormalities involving chromosomes 1 and 7, including der(1;7), are associated with myeloid neoplasms and can occur with eosinophilia.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia
Morphologic dysplasia, including irregular hypersegmented neutrophils and megaloblast-like cells
Abnormal chromosome 1 and chromosome 7 findings on karyotype
Eosinophilia with immature eosinophilic granulocyte forms in blood
Normal-to-preserved platelet count can occur in lower-risk myelodysplastic disease
Normal total leukocyte count despite abnormal differential count
symptoms_not_in_common: Very marked eosinophilia is less typical than cytopenias and multilineage dysplasia alone
Basophilia is not a usual dominant feature
Mild hypoxemia and respiratory alkalosis are not typical manifestations

data.diagnosis: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene rearrangement (for example, FIP1L1-PDGFRA-rearranged neoplasm)
data.description: A group of clonal hematologic neoplasms driven by rearrangements involving PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or related genes, commonly presenting with persistent marked eosinophilia and myeloid proliferation.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia
Circulating eosinophil precursors
Mildly elevated IgE
Anemia can occur
Basophilia can occur in a myeloproliferative neoplasm
Negative autoimmune serologies support a non-autoimmune cause of eosinophilia
symptoms_not_in_common: The shown chromosome 1 and 7 abnormality is not the classic cytogenetic pattern for PDGFRA-rearranged disease
Prominent dysplastic hypersegmented neutrophils are less characteristic
Total WBC count is not elevated despite profound relative eosinophilia
No splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms, or organ infiltration findings are provided

data.description: A diagnosis of persistent unexplained hypereosinophilia with evidence of eosinophil-related organ injury after exclusion of secondary causes and defined clonal hematologic disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia
Mildly elevated IgE
Negative ANCA, ANA, rheumatoid factor, and infectious viral markers
Mild hypoxemia could reflect possible pulmonary eosinophilic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal karyotype involving chromosomes 1 and 7 suggests a clonal hematologic disorder rather than idiopathic HES
Megaloblast-like cells and dysplastic neutrophils are not typical of idiopathic HES
Anemia is more suggestive of an underlying marrow neoplasm
Eosinophilic myelocytes and metamyelocytes in peripheral blood favor a myeloid neoplasm

data.diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia or another BCR::ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasm with eosinophilia
data.description: Myeloproliferative neoplasms can cause granulocytic proliferation with eosinophilia, basophilia, and circulating immature myeloid cells; chronic myeloid leukemia classically requires demonstration of BCR::ABL1.
symptoms_in_common: Basophilia
Eosinophilia
Circulating immature granulocytic cells
Anemia
Possible clonal cytogenetic abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: The total WBC count is not markedly elevated, unlike typical chronic myeloid leukemia
The differential is dominated by eosinophils rather than neutrophilic leukocytosis
No BCR::ABL1 result or Philadelphia chromosome finding is provided
Dysplastic eosinophil morphology and chromosome 1/7 abnormalities favor CEL or MDS-related disease over classic CML

data.description: A clonal histiocytic neoplasm characterized by proliferation of Langerhans cells, often with eosinophils, which can involve bone, skin, lungs, lymph nodes, liver, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, and kidneys. The histology and immunophenotypic appearance are most compatible with this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal abdominal and retroperitoneal soft-tissue/lymph-node lesions
Bilateral renal infiltrative or mass-like lesions
Possible pulmonary involvement on chest CT
FDG-avid multifocal disease on PET imaging
Histiocytic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
Cells with grooved/irregular nuclei compatible with Langerhans cells
Constipation and prominent stool burden/bowel distention, which may occur with gastrointestinal or abdominal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No destructive lytic bone lesions are shown
No skin rash is described
No diabetes insipidus or pituitary involvement is described

data.description: A non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder that commonly causes painless lymphadenopathy and may have extranodal involvement, including the kidneys, upper airway, skin, and gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy/soft-tissue masses
Renal involvement with bilateral infiltrative lesions
Histiocytic infiltrate on pathology
Multifocal FDG-avid lesions

No massive painless cervical lymphadenopathy is described
Possible pulmonary involvement is less typical
Constipation with stool burden is not a classic presenting feature

data.description: Lymphoma is a malignant proliferation of lymphoid cells that can present with multifocal lymphadenopathy, extranodal abdominal disease, renal infiltration, pulmonary lesions, and FDG uptake on PET.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal abdominal and retroperitoneal lymph-node/soft-tissue abnormalities
Bilateral renal infiltrative lesions
Possible thoracic or pulmonary lesion
FDG-avid multifocal disease
Bowel displacement or gastrointestinal symptoms such as constipation may occur with abdominal tumor burden
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy demonstrates a histiocytic/eosinophil-rich process rather than a monomorphic lymphoid neoplasm

No systemic B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss are provided

data.description: A non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis characterized by systemic infiltration by foamy histiocytes, often affecting long bones, retroperitoneum, kidneys, cardiovascular structures, and the central nervous system.
symptoms_in_common: Retroperitoneal soft-tissue involvement
Renal/perirenal infiltrative abnormalities
Multisystem FDG-avid disease
Histiocytic pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: The patient appears pediatric, whereas Erdheim-Chester disease is predominantly an adult disorder
No symmetric osteosclerosis of the long bones is shown
No typical perinephric 'hairy kidney' appearance is described
The histology is not described as foamy CD68-positive/CD1a-negative histiocytes

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma

data.description: Initial evaluation labs showed hemoglobin 17.6 g/dl, hematocrit 51.2%, WBC 10,060/µl with neutrophilia (9,850/µl) and lymphopenia (490/µl), and severe thrombocytopenia (24,000/µl). Chemistry showed mild hyponatremia (134 mmol/l), hypochloremia (95 mmol/l), creatinine 1.64 mg/dl, magnesium 1.1 mg/dl, elevated AST 137 U/l and ALT 119 U/l, total bilirubin 3.3 mg/dl with direct bilirubin 1.5 mg/dl, and haptoglobin <10 mg/dl. Fibrinogen was 279 mg/dl and venous pH 7.41.

A life-threatening malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, characterized by high parasitemia, intravascular hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, organ dysfunction, and potentially cerebral, renal, or hepatic complications. The blood smear shows ring-form parasites consistent with P. falciparum, including multiple rings in erythrocytes and an applique form.

Positive malaria rapid diagnostic test pattern compatible with P. falciparum
Severe thrombocytopenia (24,000/µl)
Low haptoglobin suggesting hemolysis
Hyperbilirubinemia
Elevated AST and ALT
Acute kidney injury with creatinine 1.64 mg/dl
Neutrophilia and lymphopenia
Possible splenic enlargement on abdominal ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Hemoglobin and hematocrit are elevated rather than reduced, although this may reflect hemoconcentration or early disease
Normal venous pH
Normal fibrinogen level

data.description: Adult patient with marked leukocytosis 24 days before admission and on admission: WBC 24,000/mm³ with neutrophil predominance (93.8%). data.description: Laboratory data show hypophosphatemia at presentation (phosphate 0.45 mmol/L) with elevated alkaline phosphatase (366 U/L) and elevated C-FGF23. Over 3–4 years of follow-up, phosphate stayed low to low-normal (0.53–0.65 mmol/L), calcium increased to 2.28–2.49 mmol/L, alkaline phosphatase decreased, and C-FGF23 rose markedly (1370 to 2050 U/L). Five days after resection, phosphate normalized (1.18 mmol/L), calcium was 2.39 mmol/L, alkaline phosphatase 102 U/L, and C-FGF23 decreased to 54 U/L.

data.description: Severe anemia with hematocrit 17.5%, hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL, and red-cell count 2.07 million/mm³, with reticulocytosis (7.6%) and leukocytosis (22,200/mm³). Iron level was low (19 µg/dL) with normal prothrombin time/INR and mildly low total protein/globulin.
Ongoing bleeding into the small bowel, suggested by a progressively appearing and changing focus of radiotracer activity on serial blood-pool scintigraphy.
symptoms_in_common: Severe anemia with hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL and hematocrit 17.5%
Reticulocytosis consistent with marrow response to blood loss
Low serum iron consistent with blood loss or iron depletion
Scintigraphic appearance concerning for active gastrointestinal bleeding
Leukocytosis, which may occur with physiologic stress from major hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal prothrombin time/INR is not a cause of bleeding, although it does not exclude gastrointestinal hemorrhage
Mildly low total protein/glulin is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Meckel diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa and bleeding
data.description: A congenital ileal diverticulum that can contain acid-secreting gastric mucosa, causing ulceration and significant painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding, particularly in younger patients.
symptoms_in_common: Severe anemia compatible with substantial gastrointestinal blood loss
Low iron level compatible with chronic or recurrent bleeding
Reticulocytosis compatible with active or recent blood loss
Possible small-bowel source of bleeding on scintigraphic imaging
Normal coagulation studies
symptoms_not_in_common: Leukocytosis is not a typical defining feature unless inflammation or stress is present
Mildly low total protein/globulin is not characteristic
No age, abdominal pain history, melena, hematochezia, or painless rectal bleeding is provided

data.description: Fragile dilated mucosal blood vessels, often in the small bowel or colon, that can cause intermittent occult or overt gastrointestinal bleeding and iron-deficiency anemia.

Low serum iron suggesting chronic blood loss
Reticulocytosis indicating response to blood loss
Nuclear medicine findings compatible with active gastrointestinal bleeding
Normal PT/INR, as angiodysplasia can bleed without a coagulation disorder

data.diagnosis: Nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma with pulmonary involvement
data.description: A subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma characterized histologically by broad fibrous bands dividing lymphoid tissue into nodules and scattered Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background. Pulmonary involvement can produce masses, nodules, consolidation, or rarely cavitary lesions.

Upper-lung pulmonary infiltrative/cavitary abnormality

Chronic multifocal pulmonary inflammatory changes
Small airway-centered structural abnormalities on CT

data.description: An acute or subacute recurrence of inflammatory demyelinating disease in the central nervous system. Natalizumab is commonly used to treat relapsing multiple sclerosis, so a new neurologic event in this setting may represent either an MS relapse or PML.

data.diagnosis: JC polyomavirus granule cell neuronopathy (JCPyV GCN)
data.description: A rare JCPyV-associated neurologic disorder in which the virus infects cerebellar granule neurons, producing progressive cerebellar atrophy and ataxia. It can occur in immunosuppressed patients, including those receiving natalizumab.
symptoms_in_common: Natalizumab-associated immune modulation can predispose to JCPyV central nervous system disease

data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, leading to globotriaosylceramide accumulation in the heart, kidneys, nervous system, and skin. Cardiac involvement commonly produces concentric left-ventricular hypertrophy and characteristic lamellar lysosomal inclusions ('zebra bodies') on electron microscopy.
symptoms_in_common: Electrocardiographic evidence suggestive of left-ventricular hypertrophy with repolarization abnormalities
Echocardiographic appearance consistent with marked ventricular wall thickening/concentric left-ventricular hypertrophy
Electron microscopy showing numerous lamellated intracellular lysosomal inclusions consistent with zebra bodies

symptoms_not_in_common: No noncardiac Fabry manifestations are provided, such as neuropathic burning pain, angiokeratomas, reduced sweating, corneal verticillata, proteinuria, or renal dysfunction
No family history or alpha-galactosidase A enzyme/genetic result is provided

data.description: A genetic myocardial disorder characterized by otherwise unexplained left-ventricular hypertrophy, often asymmetric, with possible diastolic dysfunction, outflow obstruction, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death risk.
symptoms_in_common: Electrocardiographic left-ventricular hypertrophy with ST-segment and T-wave abnormalities
Increased ventricular wall thickness on echocardiography
Potential cardiac hypertrophy phenotype
symptoms_not_in_common: Electron microscopy with extensive lamellar lysosomal inclusions/zebra bodies is not typical of sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
The imaging appearance suggests a storage disorder rather than isolated sarcomeric hypertrophy
No reported asymmetric septal hypertrophy, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, or dynamic left-ventricular outflow tract obstruction

data.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy-related disorder caused by LAMP2 deficiency. It can cause severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and intellectual disability, particularly in affected males.

data.description: Laboratory data show progressive anemia and severe thrombocytopenia with leukocytosis and left shift, abnormal smear findings (Döhle’s bodies, toxic granulation, polychromasia, macrocytosis, tear-drop cells, later schistocytes), prolonged PT/aPTT, hyponatremia, low bicarbonate with elevated anion gap, lactic acidosis, rising BUN/creatinine with reduced eGFR, hypoalbuminemia/low total protein, hypocalcemia, and marked AST/ALT elevation peaking at 13,090/2,373 U/L and remaining very high on later testing.

data.diagnosis: Capnocytophaga canimorsus septicemia with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and purpura fulminans
data.description: A rapidly progressive, often fulminant bloodstream infection caused by Capnocytophaga canimorsus, a dog- and cat-associated gram-negative rod. It can cause septic shock, DIC, purpura fulminans, acral ischemia/necrosis, multiorgan failure, and marked hepatic injury.

Acral cyanosis/ischemic discoloration of fingers and toes
Severe thrombocytopenia
Progressive anemia with later schistocytes

Leukocytosis with left shift, toxic granulation, and Döhle bodies consistent with severe bacterial sepsis
Lactic acidosis and elevated anion-gap metabolic acidosis
Acute kidney injury with rising BUN/creatinine and reduced eGFR
Massive AST/ALT elevation consistent with ischemic hepatitis during shock
Hypoalbuminemia, hypocalcemia, and hyponatremia during critical illness
Gram-negative rod morphology on the provided microbiology image
symptoms_not_in_common: No animal bite, scratch, dog/cat exposure, or asplenia history is provided

data.diagnosis: Purpura fulminans due to severe bacterial sepsis with disseminated intravascular coagulation

Discoloration and likely ischemia of distal extremities
Severe thrombocytopenia
Prolonged PT and aPTT
Schistocytes suggesting microangiopathic hemolysis in DIC
Progressive anemia
Acute kidney injury
Lactic acidosis
Marked transaminase elevation compatible with shock-related liver injury
Leukocytosis with toxic neutrophil changes supporting an underlying septic trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Purpura fulminans is a syndrome rather than a specific infectious organism

data.description: Laboratory abnormalities on admission at two hospitals showed elevated total bilirubin (5.8–6.7 mg/dl), markedly increased ALT/AST (ALT 85–327 U/l, AST 104–267 U/l), mildly elevated alkaline phosphatase (150–172 U/l), mildly elevated lipase (72 U/l), and increased carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (73–79 U/ml). Hemoglobin, white-cell count, platelets, electrolytes, renal function, and albumin were otherwise within normal limits.

A malignant adenocarcinoma arising from the distal common bile duct, commonly causing progressive extrahepatic biliary obstruction and jaundice. Histology typically shows infiltrating malignant glands in dense desmoplastic stroma.

Elevated ALT and AST
Mild alkaline phosphatase elevation
Elevated CA 19-9

data.description: Recent oncology-clinic labs 1 month before admission were largely normal except for mild leukopenia (WBC 3810/µL) and hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL. On admission, the patient had marked lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia (87,000/µL), acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.73 mg/dL, BUN 42 mg/dL), coagulation abnormalities (PT 16.7 sec, INR 1.4, aPTT 47.9 sec, D-dimer >10,000 ng/mL, fibrinogen 135 mg/dL), and elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin (AST 190 U/L, ALT 62 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 173 U/L, bilirubin 1.9 mg/dL), with elevated CK (1679 U/L) and abnormal urinalysis showing blood and protein. By hospital day 5, creatinine and coagulation tests improved, but anemia worsened (hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL), thrombocytopenia persisted (99,000/µL), and liver tests remained elevated (AST 407 U/L, ALT 138 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 510 U/L, bilirubin 2.6 mg/dL).

data.description: An autosomal-dominant vascular dysplasia characterized by mucocutaneous telangiectasias and visceral arteriovenous malformations, especially in the lungs, brain, liver, and gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation visible on chest CT
Intracranial vascular malformation demonstrated on MR angiography/catheter angiography
Multiple cerebral lesions compatible with embolic ischemic complications
Possible paradoxical embolic complications from a right-to-left shunt through a pulmonary AVM
symptoms_not_in_common: No epistaxis is described
No mucocutaneous telangiectasias are described
No family history of HHT is provided
No gastrointestinal bleeding or iron-deficiency anemia is described

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation with paradoxical cerebral embolization
data.description: A direct abnormal connection between a pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein that creates a right-to-left shunt, allowing thrombi, air, or septic material to bypass the pulmonary capillary filter and reach the cerebral circulation.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary vascular nodule with feeding and draining vessels on chest CT
Multiple acute diffusion-restricting cerebral lesions consistent with embolic infarcts
Potential intracranial hemorrhagic or embolic lesion
Brain involvement in multiple vascular territories, which can occur with paradoxical emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: No dyspnea is described
No hypoxemia or cyanosis is reported
No platypnea-orthodeoxia symptoms are reported
No documented venous thrombosis or embolic source is provided

data.description: A congenital high-flow vascular lesion consisting of direct artery-to-vein connections without an intervening capillary bed. Brain AVMs can cause intracranial hemorrhage, seizures, focal neurologic deficits, or ischemic complications.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal intracranial vascular nidus/shunting pattern on angiographic imaging
Prominent abnormal cerebral vessels on MR angiography
Possible hemorrhagic focus on T2-weighted imaging
Cerebral ischemic lesions that may occur from vascular steal or embolic phenomena
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache is described
No seizures are described
No focal neurologic deficits are explicitly reported
A pulmonary AVM is not a typical feature of an isolated sporadic brain AVM

data.diagnosis: Cerebral septic emboli or brain abscess related to a pulmonary right-to-left shunt
data.description: Patients with pulmonary AVMs are predisposed to cerebral septic emboli and brain abscess because bacteria can bypass normal pulmonary capillary filtration through the right-to-left shunt.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple intracranial lesions with diffusion restriction
A focal lesion with a possible hemorrhagic or ring-like appearance
Pulmonary AVM, which is a recognized risk factor for brain abscess and septic cerebral emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever is described
No leukocytosis or inflammatory-marker elevation is provided
No bacteremia or systemic infection is reported
No headache, altered mental status, or meningeal symptoms are described

data.description: A systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease characterized by noncaseating granulomas, commonly involving hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes and the lungs.
symptoms_in_common: FDG-avid bilateral hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy on PET imaging
Pulmonary nodular/interstitial abnormalities
Biopsy showing noncaseating granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes and giant cells
No obvious destructive lung mass on CT

data.description: A mycobacterial infection that can cause granulomatous inflammation and thoracic lymphadenopathy, usually with caseating necrosis and often upper-lung involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Mediastinal and hilar lymph node enlargement
Granulomatous inflammation on tissue pathology
Pulmonary imaging abnormalities
FDG uptake in inflammatory lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology appears to show noncaseating rather than caseating granulomas
No reported cavitation, tree-in-bud nodules, or upper-lobe destructive disease
No reported fever, night sweats, weight loss, productive cough, or tuberculosis exposure

data.description: A malignancy of lymphocytes that may present with intensely FDG-avid mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy; granulomatous reactions can occasionally occur adjacent to lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: FDG-avid mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy
Thoracic lymph node enlargement on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy demonstrates granulomatous inflammation rather than a malignant lymphoid proliferation
No reported bulky nodal mass or widespread nodal/extranodal disease
No reported B symptoms such as unexplained fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.diagnosis: Fungal granulomatous infection, such as histoplasmosis
data.description: Certain fungal infections can produce granulomas and mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy, sometimes mimicking sarcoidosis on PET and CT imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous inflammation on biopsy
Hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Pulmonary abnormalities
FDG-avid inflammatory lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fungal organisms on pathology or microbiologic testing
No reported necrotizing granulomas
No reported exposure history to endemic fungal regions, bird or bat droppings, or immunosuppression
No reported fever, cough, or constitutional infectious symptoms

An inherited osteoclast dysfunction disorder causing failure of normal bone resorption, diffuse osteosclerosis, very high bone mineral density, and structurally abnormal but potentially brittle bone.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated lumbar-spine bone mineral density (T-score 7.1)
Markedly elevated femoral-neck bone mineral density (T-score 5.1)
Diffuse increased skeletal density on pelvic radiograph
Abnormal dense trabecular bone architecture
Histologic appearance consistent with retained or poorly remodeled bone
symptoms_not_in_common: No fractures are described
No anemia, thrombocytopenia, or marrow-failure findings are described
No cranial-nerve compression symptoms such as visual or hearing loss are described
No hepatosplenomegaly is described

data.diagnosis: Osteopetrosis due to carbonic anhydrase II deficiency
data.description: A recessive form of osteopetrosis caused by impaired osteoclast acidification, usually associated with osteosclerosis, cerebral calcification, renal tubular acidosis, and developmental impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Extremely high bone mineral density
Diffuse pelvic osteosclerosis
Abnormal bone remodeling on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal tubular acidosis is not described
Intracranial calcifications are not described
Developmental delay is not described
Growth failure is not described
Fractures are not described

data.diagnosis: High-bone-mass syndrome due to LRP5 gain-of-function mutation
data.description: A genetic high-bone-mass disorder caused by increased Wnt signaling and enhanced bone formation, producing very high DXA values and generalized osteosclerosis, often without marrow failure.
symptoms_in_common: Very high lumbar-spine bone mineral density
Very high femoral-neck bone mineral density
Generalized increased bone density on radiograph
No reported hematologic or marrow-failure manifestations
symptoms_not_in_common: Craniofacial thickening is not described
Mandibular enlargement is not described
Torus palatinus or other bony overgrowth is not described
Cranial-nerve compression symptoms are not described
The histologic suggestion of impaired bone resorption is more typical of osteopetrosis

data.description: A metabolic bone disorder caused by chronic excessive fluoride exposure, leading to diffuse osteosclerosis, increased bone density, calcification of ligaments, and sometimes bone pain or stiffness.
symptoms_in_common: Increased bone mineral density
Diffuse osteosclerotic appearance of the pelvis
Abnormal bone structure on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Fluoride exposure history is not described
Ligament or tendon calcification is not described
Joint stiffness or chronic bone pain is not described
Dental fluorosis is not described
The extremely high DXA values and histologic remodeling abnormality may be more suggestive of an inherited high-bone-mass disorder

data.description: Hipernatremia e hipercloremia marcadas en la presentación (Na 164 mmol/L, Cl 124 mmol/L), con osmolalidad sérica elevada (334 mOsm/kg) y BUN ligeramente elevado, mejorando en 3 días (Na 160 mmol/L). Las anomalías hormonales incluyeron testosterona muy baja, baja hormona luteinizante y hormona folículo-estimulante, prolactina elevada, tiroxina libre baja con TSH normal, cortisol bajo e IGF-1 bajo. Los lípidos mostraron colesterol total elevado y LDL. El LCR estaba limpio con pleocitosis leve y proteínas elevadas; la citología no mostró células malignas. El sodio urinario fue de 64 mmol/L con osmolalidad urinaria de 314 mOsm/kg.

Un tumor primario de células germinales del sistema nervioso central que suele surgir en la región pineal o suprasellar y puede afectar al hipotálamo y al tallo pituitario, causando diabetes insípida y deficiencias hormonales de la hipófisis anterior. Pueden producirse lesiones multifocales que aumentan la línea media.
symptoms_in_common: Hipernatremia marcada y osmolalidad sérica elevada compatibles con diabetes insípida central
Osmolalidad urinaria que es insuficientemente baja en relación con una hipernatremia severa
Patrón de panhipopituitarismo: testosterona baja con LH y FSH bajos, tiroxina libre baja con TSH inadecuadamente normal, cortisol bajo e IGF-1 bajo
Prolactina elevada compatible con disfunción hipofisaria/hipotalámica
Lesiones hipotalámicas-supraselares y posibles lesiones multifocales de realce de la línea media en la resonancia magnética
Puede producirse pleocitosis leve de LCR y una elevación de la proteína del LCR
La citología negativa de LCR no excluye el germinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: El LDL elevado y el colesterol total son inespecíficos y no constituyen una característica definitoria
Una ligera elevación del BUN es más probable que sea secundaria a la deshidratación que al propio tumor

data.diagnosis: Linfoma primario del sistema nervioso central que afecta al hipotálamo y al tallo hipofisario
data.description: El linfoma primario del SNC es un tumor linfoide maligno que puede presentarse con lesiones cerebrales fuertemente potenciadas y, al afectar la región hipotalámica-hipofisaria, puede producir diabetes insípida central e hipopituitarismo.
symptoms_in_common: Aumento de las lesiones intracraneales que afectan a la región hipotalámico-hipofisaria
Fisiología central de la diabetes insípida con hipernatremia y hiperosmolalidad severas
Deficiencias de la hormona anteropofisaria
Hiperprolactinemia por alteración del tallo hipofisario
Puede aparecer pleocitosis leve de LCR y una elevación de la proteína del LCR
La citología del LCR puede ser negativa a pesar del linfoma del SNC
symptoms_not_in_common: La distribución suprasela-pineal multifocal en línea media es más característica del germinoma que del linfoma
No se han reportado manifestaciones de linfoma sistémico
El colesterol elevado y el LDL no son características típicas que se presenten

data.diagnosis: Neurosarcoidosis que afecta al eje hipotalámico-hipófisis
data.description: La neurosarcoidosis es una inflamación granulomatosa del sistema nervioso que puede infiltrarse en el hipotálamo, el tallo hipofisario, las meninges y las vías ópticas. Puede causar diabetes insípida central, hiperprolactinemia y múltiples deficiencias anterohipófisis.
symptoms_in_common: Patrón central de diabetes insípida con hipernatremia, hiperosmolalidad y orina inadecuadamente concentrada
Hipopituitarismo que afecta a los ejes gonadal, tiroideo, suprarrenal y hormona del crecimiento
Prolactina elevada debido a afectación del tallo o hipotálamo
Realce del tallo hipotalámico-hipofisario en la imagen
Pleocitosis leve de LCR y proteína elevada
symptoms_not_in_common: No se han reportado hallazgos pulmonares, ganglios linfáticos, cutáneos, oculares o sistémicos
Las masas intracraneales multifocales discretas pueden ser menos comunes que las masas meníngeas o predominantes en el tallo
La citología negativa de LCR no es especialmente informativa para la sarcoidosis
La hiperlipidemia no es una característica característica

data.diagnosis: Histiocitosis de células de Langerhans con afectación hipotalámica-hipofisaria
data.description: La histiocitosis de células de Langerhan es un trastorno histiocítico clonal que puede infiltrarse en el tallo hipofisario y el hipotálamo. La diabetes insípida central es una presentación endocrina común, y puede desarrollarse disfunción hipofisaria anterior.
symptoms_in_common: Hipernatremia severa e hiperosmolalidad compatibles con diabetes insípida central
Deficiencias hormonales de la hipófisis que incluyen hipogonadismo central, hipotiroidismo central, cortisol bajo y IGF-1 bajo
Prolactina elevada por afectación del tallo hipofisario
Tallo hipofisario/lesión hipotalámica en la resonancia magnética
symptoms_not_in_common: No se han reportado lesiones óseas, antecedentes de poliuria/polidipsia relacionados con la diabetes, erupciones cutáneas, enfermedades pulmonares u otras manifestaciones sistémicas de histiocitosis de células de Langerhans
Las lesiones cerebrales multifocales y profundas de mejora son menos comunes que la implicación aislada del tallo
La pleocitosis leve del LCR y el aumento de la proteína del LCR no son hallazgos clásicos
La hiperlipidemia no es típica

data.description: A rare congenital cardiac anomaly in which a fibromuscular membrane divides the left atrium into a pulmonary venous chamber and a distal chamber connected to the mitral valve, causing variable obstruction to pulmonary venous flow.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic appearance of a membrane within the left atrium
Appearance of a fenestration/opening in the atrial membrane
Notched or broad P-wave morphology consistent with left atrial enlargement
Findings that may mimic mitral stenosis

data.description: A congenital membrane located immediately above the mitral valve that obstructs inflow from the left atrium to the left ventricle and can resemble congenital mitral stenosis.
symptoms_in_common: Left atrial membrane seen on echocardiography
Possible left atrial enlargement suggested by notched P waves
Potential obstruction to mitral inflow
symptoms_not_in_common: The membrane appears to divide the left atrium rather than being confined directly above the mitral valve

data.description: Narrowing of the mitral valve, most commonly rheumatic in origin, leading to impaired left atrial emptying, left atrial enlargement, and pulmonary venous congestion.
symptoms_in_common: Notched P waves that can indicate left atrial enlargement (P mitrale)
Possible physiology of impaired flow from the left atrium toward the mitral valve
symptoms_not_in_common: An intra-left-atrial membrane is not a typical finding of isolated mitral stenosis
No definite thickened, calcified, or fused mitral valve leaflets are shown

data.description: A benign primary cardiac tumor, usually arising from the interatrial septum, that can intermittently obstruct the mitral valve and produce symptoms similar to mitral stenosis.
symptoms_in_common: Potential left atrial obstruction
Possible left atrial enlargement with notched P-wave morphology
symptoms_not_in_common: The echocardiographic finding appears membranous rather than a mobile discrete mass
No pedunculated tumor attached to the interatrial septum is evident

data.diagnosis: Infantile-onset Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II)
data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) deficiency, resulting in lysosomal glycogen accumulation, especially in cardiac and skeletal muscle. Classic infantile disease causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hypotonia, weakness, and respiratory failure.
symptoms_in_common: Infant chest radiograph with apparent cardiomegaly/enlarged cardiac silhouette
Laboratory image showing abnormal or markedly reduced mature GAA protein processing/expression
Early-life presentation compatible with severe infantile metabolic cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as hypotonia, feeding difficulty, macroglossia, respiratory distress, or muscle weakness were provided

data.description: A disorder characterized by abnormal thickening of the heart muscle, which may be genetic, metabolic, or secondary to conditions such as Pompe disease. In infants it can cause cardiomegaly, heart failure, and poor feeding.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent enlarged cardiac silhouette on chest radiograph
Infant age group is compatible with presentation of metabolic or genetic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal GAA precursor/mature protein pattern is not typical of isolated sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
No reported murmur, heart failure, poor feeding, sweating with feeds, cyanosis, or family history

data.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy-related disorder caused by LAMP2 deficiency. It commonly causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and intellectual disability, usually with a later childhood or adolescent presentation than classic infantile Pompe disease.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac enlargement compatible with cardiomyopathy
Potential skeletal-muscle involvement is possible in lysosomal myopathies
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) processing is not characteristic of Danon disease
Severe neonatal/early-infantile presentation is less typical
No reported developmental delay, cognitive impairment, or documented skeletal myopathy

data.description: A group of genetic disorders affecting mitochondrial energy production that can present in infancy with hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy, hypotonia, lactic acidosis, and multisystem disease.
symptoms_in_common: Possible infantile cardiomyopathy suggested by the enlarged cardiac silhouette
Early infancy can be a presentation period for severe metabolic cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: The abnormal GAA precursor/mature protein finding specifically favors a lysosomal GAA disorder rather than a primary mitochondrial disorder
No reported lactic acidosis, neurologic abnormalities, seizures, liver dysfunction, or metabolic decompensation

data.description: Progressive anemia over 1 year: hematocrit 35.6% and hemoglobin 12.0 g/dl, declining to 30.9% and 10.6 g/dl on admission, with microcytosis (MCV 75 fL). ESR was elevated and increased from 41 to 66 mm/hr, with elevated CRP (8.3 mg/dl). LDH (517 U/l) and ferritin (470 ng/ml) were elevated. Reticulocytes were 3.0%, PT 14.4 sec, INR 1.2. White blood cell count and platelets were within normal range on admission. Borrelia burgdorferi antibodies were negative.

An aggressive neoplasm of immature B-cell lymphoblasts that may present as extranodal soft-tissue, renal, nodal, or marrow disease. It is termed leukemia when there is substantial bone-marrow or peripheral-blood involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive anemia
Elevated LDH
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR and CRP)
Imaging evidence of multifocal hypermetabolic soft-tissue/extranodal lesions
Renal and pelvic/soft-tissue lesions on CT/PET imaging
Histologic appearance of a blastic hematolymphoid neoplasm
Flow-cytometry pattern consistent with B-cell lineage, including CD19 and CD10 expression
Normal peripheral white blood cell count can occur in lymphoblastic lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic anemia is less typical than normocytic anemia from marrow involvement or inflammation
Ferritin elevation is nonspecific and not diagnostic
No reported leukocytosis or circulating blasts

data.description: A highly aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that frequently involves extranodal organs, particularly the abdomen, kidneys, bone marrow, and central nervous system.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated LDH suggesting high tumor turnover
Anemia
Extranodal abdominal and renal lesions on imaging
Hypermetabolic lesions on PET imaging
B-cell marker expression such as CD19
Possible marrow involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: CD10 positivity can occur, but the reported blastic morphology and immature B-cell phenotype favor lymphoblastic lymphoma rather than Burkitt lymphoma
Progression over approximately one year is slower than the usual very rapid course of untreated Burkitt lymphoma
No reported bulky abdominal mass, bowel obstruction, or tumor-lysis syndrome
Normal white blood cell count and platelets are less suggestive of extensive marrow disease

data.description: The most common aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma, often presenting with nodal or extranodal masses and systemic inflammation; renal, soft-tissue, and marrow involvement may occur.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive anemia
Elevated ESR and CRP
Elevated LDH
Multifocal extranodal and hypermetabolic lesions on CT/PET imaging
B-cell lineage marker expression, including CD19
Normal peripheral white blood cell count may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent lymphoblast-like morphology and CD10-positive precursor phenotype are less typical than a mature large B-cell phenotype
No reported bulky lymphadenopathy
Microcytic anemia is not a characteristic presentation
No reported constitutional B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.diagnosis: Myeloid sarcoma associated with acute myeloid leukemia
data.description: A tumor mass of immature myeloid blasts occurring outside the bone marrow, which can involve skin, lymph nodes, bone, soft tissues, kidneys, and other organs; it may precede detectable acute myeloid leukemia in blood.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia
Elevated LDH
Multifocal soft-tissue and extranodal lesions
Possible renal involvement
Blastic cellular morphology on tissue examination
Normal peripheral white blood cell count can occur before overt leukemia
symptoms_not_in_common: B-cell marker expression, particularly CD19 and CD10, favors B-lymphoblastic lymphoma rather than myeloid sarcoma
No reported myeloid-marker profile such as myeloperoxidase, CD13, CD33, or CD117 positivity
No reported circulating myeloblasts
Normal platelet and white blood cell counts make overt acute myeloid leukemia less likely

data.description: A bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous breast tissue causing diffuse inflammation; ultrasound commonly shows skin thickening and subcutaneous edema without a drainable collection.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral diffuse breast erythema
Breast swelling
Apparent skin thickening
Subcutaneous edema and inflammatory change on ultrasound
No discrete fluid collection on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic symptoms are provided
No drainage or skin ulceration is visible

data.description: An aggressive form of breast cancer in which tumor emboli obstruct dermal lymphatics, producing rapid breast redness, edema, enlargement, and peau d'orange-like skin changes.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral breast erythema
Diffuse breast enlargement or swelling
Skin thickening
Edematous appearance of the breast skin and subcutaneous tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: The ultrasound appearance shown is more suggestive of diffuse inflammatory edema than a defined underlying malignant mass
No nipple retraction, breast mass, peau d'orange, or axillary lymphadenopathy is described

data.description: A localized collection of pus within breast tissue, usually developing as a complication of mastitis or cellulitis and often causing focal pain, fluctuance, and fever.
symptoms_in_common: Breast erythema
Breast swelling
Inflammatory changes in subcutaneous tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete fluid collection or drainable cavity is visible on ultrasound
The erythema appears diffuse rather than centered over a focal fluctuant mass
No purulent drainage is described

data.diagnosis: Breast hematoma or traumatic breast contusion
data.description: Bleeding into breast soft tissues after trauma, surgery, anticoagulant use, or a procedure; it may cause swelling, bruising, and tenderness.
symptoms_in_common: Localized breast swelling
Reddish-purple discoloration that can resemble bruising
Diffuse soft-tissue abnormality on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: The marked erythema and skin thickening are more typical of infection or inflammatory edema than an uncomplicated hematoma
No well-defined complex fluid collection compatible with a hematoma is shown
No trauma, procedure, or anticoagulant exposure is provided

data.diagnosis: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome)
data.description: A severe delayed drug-hypersensitivity reaction characterized by a widespread rash, prominent facial edema, fever, eosinophilia, lymphadenopathy, and possible internal-organ involvement such as hepatitis or nephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Marked facial swelling and erythema
Diffuse erythematous papular or morbilliform rash on the chest and upper extremities
Swelling and rash involving the hands
Widespread skin eruption
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, eosinophilia, lymph-node enlargement, or organ involvement is provided

data.description: A common medication-related exanthem causing a symmetric, widespread red maculopapular rash, usually beginning on the trunk and spreading to the limbs; facial involvement may occur.
symptoms_in_common: Symmetric diffuse red rash over the chest
Maculopapular-appearing eruption on the arms and hands
Facial erythema
Generalized distribution of rash
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent facial and hand swelling is more suggestive of a severe drug reaction than an uncomplicated morbilliform eruption

data.description: An acute medication-triggered skin reaction with widespread erythema and many small sterile pustules, often accompanied by fever and neutrophilia; edema of the face may occur.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse erythematous eruption on the trunk and extremities
Facial redness and swelling
Possible small superficial pustular lesions within the rash
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinct widespread nonfollicular pustules are not clearly visible
No acute fever or laboratory evidence of neutrophilia is provided

data.description: A delayed immune-mediated reaction, often caused by medications, that can produce rash, swelling of the hands or face, fever, and joint pain.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse rash
Edema of the hands
Facial swelling and erythema
symptoms_not_in_common: Joint pain, fever, and lymph-node enlargement are not described

data.description: Keratoacanthomas are rapidly growing crateriform keratinizing skin tumors that may regress spontaneously but can resemble well-differentiated cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Eruptive forms cause numerous recurrent lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous papules and nodules on the hands and forearms
Crateriform hyperkeratotic and ulcerated lesions
Histology reported as 15 keratoacanthomas
Progressive development of new lesions
Partial improvement with topical imiquimod and 5-fluorouracil
No metastatic disease on computed tomography
symptoms_not_in_common: Coexisting lesions diagnosed as verruca vulgaris
Marked isomorphic/Koebner-like response after procedures or trauma

data.diagnosis: Multiple self-healing squamous epithelioma of Ferguson-Smith
data.description: A rare inherited or sporadic eruptive keratoacanthoma disorder characterized by repeated crops of locally destructive keratoacanthoma-like tumors that eventually involute, often leaving scars.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple recurrent keratoacanthoma-like tumors
Lesions with ulceration and central keratin/crater formation
Progressive appearance of lesions over months to years
Scarring and post-inflammatory color changes after lesions
Absence of detected metastases despite numerous tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: Disease appears concentrated mainly on one upper extremity rather than involving many body sites
No family history or spontaneous regression of individual lesions is provided
Coexisting verruca vulgaris is not a defining feature

data.description: A rare eruptive keratoacanthoma syndrome with many small keratinizing papules that continuously arise over time, often on sun-exposed skin and potentially involving the face and mucous membranes.
symptoms_in_common: Eruptive onset of many keratoacanthoma-like papules and nodules
Histologic confirmation of multiple keratoacanthomas
Ongoing formation of lesions over time
Hyperkeratotic, crusted, and ulcerated lesions
Some response to topical antitumor therapies such as imiquimod and 5-fluorouracil
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are predominantly limited to the upper extremities
No facial involvement, mask-like facies, ectropion, or mucosal lesions are described
Lesions are larger and more ulcerated than the typical numerous tiny papules of Grzybowski syndrome

data.diagnosis: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma-type, multifocal
data.description: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a malignant keratinocyte tumor that can present as rapidly enlarging hyperkeratotic nodules or ulcers. Keratoacanthoma-type lesions may be difficult to distinguish histologically and clinically from benign keratoacanthomas.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple persistent hyperkeratotic nodules and ulcerated plaques
Crusted lesions on sun-exposed dorsal hands and forearms
Histology with keratoacanthoma-like squamous proliferation
Progressive disease without treatment
Clinical use of 5-fluorouracil and imiquimod for superficial keratinocytic neoplasia
Imaging performed to exclude metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high number of lesions developing in an eruptive pattern is less typical of sporadic squamous cell carcinoma
No metastases or lymphadenopathy were identified
Some lesions were classified as verruca vulgaris rather than carcinoma

data.description: A fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) within the spinal cord, often extending over multiple spinal levels and appearing bright on T2-weighted MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Intramedullary central T2-bright fluid-signal cavity in the cervical/thoracic spinal cord on MRI

data.diagnosis: Hydromyelia (persistent dilatation of the central canal)
data.description: Dilatation of the spinal cord's normal central canal containing cerebrospinal fluid; it may be asymptomatic and can resemble a small syrinx on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Small midline fluid-signal cavity following the central canal within the spinal cord
Cervical and thoracic spinal cord involvement on sagittal MRI

data.description: Syringomyelia caused by impaired cerebrospinal-fluid circulation at the craniovertebral junction, commonly associated with downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils.
symptoms_in_common: Spinal cord syrinx-like T2-bright cavity
symptoms_not_in_common: Cerebellar tonsillar descent is not clearly demonstrated on the provided images
No headache, neck pain, sensory loss, weakness, or other clinical symptoms were provided

data.description: An acute precursor B-cell neoplasm characterized by marrow and peripheral-blood replacement by lymphoblasts. The images show blast-rich marrow and a complex X;14 rearrangement involving Xq22.3, where IRS4 is located, and chromosome 14, consistent with an IGH-associated IRS4 rearrangement.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral blood smear showing circulating immature blast-like cells
Bone marrow extensively infiltrated by lymphoblasts
Monomorphic population of small-to-medium blasts with scant cytoplasm
Cytogenetic evidence of a translocation involving chromosome X and chromosome 14
FISH evidence of rearrangement involving the IRS4 region at Xq22.3
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms or physical examination findings are provided
No documented B-cell immunophenotype is provided
No documented cytopenia values, fever, bleeding, lymphadenopathy, or hepatosplenomegaly are provided

data.description: An aggressive neoplasm of immature T-cell precursors that commonly presents with marrow and blood blasts and may have chromosomal rearrangements involving chromosome 14, particularly the T-cell receptor alpha/delta locus at 14q11.2.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral blood blasts
Bone marrow packed with immature lymphoid-appearing blasts
Chromosome 14 involvement in a complex rearrangement
Morphology compatible with acute lymphoblastic leukemia
symptoms_not_in_common: The illustrated chromosome 14 breakpoint appears more compatible with a 14q32/IGH-region rearrangement than the usual TCRAD locus at 14q11.2

data.diagnosis: Isolated cortical vein thrombosis with venous infarction

data.description: Recent cardiac arrest with marked laboratory abnormalities: anemia, leukocytosis with neutrophilia and bands, hypoalbuminemia and low total protein, hypocalcemia, elevated AST/ALT, prolonged PTT, markedly elevated troponin T and creatine kinase/CK-MB, and hyperglycemia. Arterial blood gas showed acidosis before transfer (pH 7.19) that improved on arrival (pH 7.31). Hemoglobin fell to 9.6 g/dL, WBC rose to 19,500/µL, AST increased to 648 U/L, ALT to 101 U/L, troponin T to 28.32 ng/mL, CK to 11,012 U/L, and CK-MB to 552 U/L on arrival.

data.diagnosis: Massive acute pulmonary embolism with acute right-heart strain
data.description: Obstruction of the pulmonary arterial circulation by thrombus, causing acute right-ventricular failure, hypoxemia, shock, cardiac arrest, and myocardial injury from severe right-heart strain.
symptoms_in_common: Recent cardiac arrest
Acidosis before transfer
Marked troponin T and CK-MB elevation from myocardial strain/injury
Tachycardic ECG appearance with right-heart strain features
Echocardiographic appearance concerning for right-ventricular dysfunction/strain
Bilateral dependent pulmonary opacities and pleural effusions that may occur with shock, pulmonary infarction, or edema
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia, which can occur as a stress response
Elevated AST and ALT compatible with ischemic hepatitis from shock
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia is not a typical direct manifestation
Hypoalbuminemia and low total protein are not specific for acute pulmonary embolism
Marked CK elevation may exceed what is expected from pulmonary embolism alone and may reflect resuscitation-related rhabdomyolysis
Prolonged PTT is not intrinsic to pulmonary embolism and may reflect anticoagulation or coagulopathy

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
