data.diagnosis: Classical homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency
data.description: An autosomal-recessive disorder of transsulfuration causing markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine. It commonly produces ectopia lentis, marfanoid skeletal features, osteoporosis, and thromboembolic risk.
symptoms_in_common: Extremely elevated plasma homocysteine (237.0 umol/L)
Markedly elevated methionine (240 nmol/mL)
Normal methylmalonic acid
Normal vitamin B12 and folic acid levels
Lens subluxation/dislocation visible on eye imaging
Marfanoid facial and skeletal appearance
Pectus deformity
Low bone mineral density
Vertebral compression/biconcave vertebral changes consistent with osteoporosis

data.description: A connective-tissue disorder, usually caused by pathogenic variants in FBN1, characterized by marfanoid body habitus, chest-wall deformity, skeletal abnormalities, and lens dislocation.
symptoms_in_common: Marfanoid facial and skeletal appearance
Pectus deformity
Lens subluxation/dislocation
Reduced bone density and vertebral skeletal abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely elevated homocysteine
Markedly elevated methionine
Normal methylmalonic acid in the setting of severe hyperhomocysteinemia

data.diagnosis: Remethylation disorder causing homocystinuria (for example, MTHFR deficiency or cobalamin metabolism defect)
data.description: Inherited defects of homocysteine remethylation can cause severe hyperhomocysteinemia, often with neurologic, developmental, hematologic, or thrombotic manifestations. Unlike CBS deficiency, methionine is usually low or normal.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine
Normal serum vitamin B12 and folate can occur in inherited intracellular cobalamin-processing defects
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated methionine, which is atypical because remethylation disorders usually lower methionine
Normal methylmalonic acid, which argues against many cobalamin metabolism defects
Lens subluxation and marfanoid skeletal phenotype are less typical
Pectus deformity and severe osteoporosis are less typical

data.diagnosis: Brainstem cavernous malformation (pontine cavernoma) causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: A cavernous malformation is a cluster of abnormal, low-flow blood vessels that can bleed repeatedly. A lesion in the pons or dorsal brainstem can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow through the fourth ventricle or cerebral aqueduct, producing hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Hyperdense focal lesion in the pons/brainstem on CT, compatible with blood products or calcification
Focal brainstem lesion on MRI
Dilated lateral ventricles consistent with hydrocephalus
Possible obstruction near the fourth ventricle/brainstem cerebrospinal-fluid pathways
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as acute headache, vomiting, diplopia, facial weakness, limb weakness, ataxia, or altered consciousness were provided
No definite MRI description of the classic mixed-signal 'popcorn' appearance or hemosiderin rim was provided

data.diagnosis: Brainstem hemorrhage with intraventricular cerebrospinal-fluid obstruction
data.description: A small hemorrhage in the pons or adjacent fourth-ventricular region may obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid circulation and lead to acute or subacute obstructive hydrocephalus. Causes include hypertension, vascular malformation, or hemorrhagic tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Hyperdense lesion within the pons on noncontrast CT, which may represent acute or subacute blood
Ventricular enlargement indicating hydrocephalus
Lesion location near the fourth ventricle and posterior fossa cerebrospinal-fluid pathways
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported sudden severe headache
No reported decreased level of consciousness
No reported vomiting, cranial-nerve palsies, coma, or severe motor deficits
No extensive acute hemorrhage or major mass effect is evident from the provided images

data.description: Ependymoma is a glial tumor that can arise from the lining of the fourth ventricle or nearby brainstem. It may obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow and cause enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior fossa/brainstem-region abnormality
Hydrocephalus with enlargement of the lateral ventricles
Potential obstruction at the fourth ventricle or aqueductal level
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears small and focal rather than a typical expansile fourth-ventricular mass
No described heterogeneous enhancing tumor component
No reported progressive headache, nausea, vomiting, gait disturbance, or papilledema
No reported cranial-nerve dysfunction or cerebellar signs

data.description: No age or sex stated. Over the first 4 hospital days, the patient had anemia with falling hematocrit/hemoglobin (41.3%/14.6 g/dl to 37.9%/13.0 g/dl), reticulocytopenia, leukopenia (7,100 to 2,200/mm3) with an initial neutrophil predominance shifting to lymphocyte predominance, and thrombocytopenia (126,000 to 75,000–84,000/mm3). Inflammatory markers were markedly elevated (CRP 120.9–178.5 mg/L, ferritin 8,343 to 7,008 ng/ml), with elevated LDH, AST/ALT, and triglycerides. Mild hyponatremia and low calcium/total protein were also present. Iron studies showed low iron and low iron-binding capacity.

Leukopenia

Elevated LDH

data.description: Progressive jawbone necrosis associated with antiresorptive or antiangiogenic medications, often causing exposed devitalized bone, infection, fistulae, and pathologic fracture.

Ulcerated and inflamed oral mucosa adjacent to necrotic bone
Extensive destructive changes of the maxilla and mandible on CT

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome type 8)
data.description: A rare autosomal-dominant calcium-channel disorder caused by pathogenic CACNA1C variants, classically p.Gly406Arg. It causes marked QT prolongation, functional 2:1 atrioventricular block, ventricular arrhythmias, and characteristic hand/foot syndactyly.

data.description: Outpatient clinic day before admission and on admission labs showed marked leukocytosis (WBC 146,700–145,400/mm3) with severe eosinophilia (70–83%; absolute eosinophils 120,690/mm3), mild basophilia, and thrombocytosis (440,000–483,000/mm3). On admission, PT was prolonged (16.3 sec), sodium 133 mmol/L, glucose 44 mg/dL, albumin 3.2 g/dL, phosphorus 2.4 mg/dL, calcium 8.4 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 232 U/L, AST 163 U/L, and LDH 322 U/L.

Microcytic anemia is not specific for giant cell arteritis

data.diagnosis: Infectious aortitis or mycotic aortic aneurysm
data.description: Infection of the aortic wall, usually bacterial, causing intense inflammation, wall destruction, pseudoaneurysm or aneurysm formation, and potentially valvular involvement or regurgitation.
symptoms_in_common: Marked leukocytosis with neutrophilia
Markedly elevated CRP and ESR
Hypoalbuminemia
Anemia
Thrombocytosis as an inflammatory response
Aortic wall and luminal abnormalities on imaging
Possible aortic valve regurgitation if infection involves the aortic root or valve
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, positive blood cultures, bacteremia, focal infectious source, or septic embolic findings are provided
Diffuse long-segment stenotic arterial disease is less typical of infectious aortitis than of inflammatory large-vessel vasculitis
Microcytosis suggests a more chronic anemia pattern than an acute isolated infection

data.description: A systemic inflammatory vasculitis that can affect arteries and veins of all sizes; arterial involvement may cause aortitis, aneurysms, pseudoaneurysms, thrombosis, and aortic valve regurgitation.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP
Leukocytosis
Anemia
Thrombocytosis
Hypoalbuminemia
Aortic inflammatory abnormalities on imaging
Possible aortic regurgitation due to inflammatory involvement of the aortic root
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, skin lesions, arthritis, or venous thrombosis are reported
The imaging pattern of diffuse arterial narrowing is more characteristic of Takayasu arteritis than Behçet-related vascular disease

data.description: A fibroinflammatory immune-mediated disorder that can involve the aorta and its branches, causing aortic wall thickening, periaortic soft tissue, aneurysm formation, stenosis, and occasionally involvement of other organs.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory-marker elevation
Anemia and hypoalbuminemia in systemic inflammatory disease
Aortic wall abnormalities on imaging
Potential involvement of the abdominal aorta and branch vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: The marked neutrophilic leukocytosis and very high CRP are less typical for IgG4-related disease
No pancreatic, salivary gland, orbital, renal, retroperitoneal, or other characteristic IgG4-related organ involvement is described
Aortic regurgitation and extensive stenotic large-vessel disease are less typical than in Takayasu arteritis

data.description: A congenital abnormal rotation/fixation of the bowel that can allow the small intestine and mesentery to twist around the superior mesenteric vessels, producing the CT whirlpool sign and potentially causing bowel obstruction or ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Whirling/twisting appearance of mesenteric fat and vessels around the superior mesenteric artery
Abnormal mesenteric vessel configuration
Appearance compatible with small-bowel mesenteric twisting
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, or inability to pass stool/gas were provided

data.description: Twisting of a segment of small bowel and its mesentery around the mesenteric vascular pedicle, which may cause closed-loop obstruction and compromise bowel blood supply.
symptoms_in_common: CT whirlpool sign involving mesenteric vessels and mesenteric fat
Twisted appearance of small-bowel mesentery
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite dilated small-bowel loops or clear transition point is provided
No reported acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distention, or bowel ischemia symptoms

data.description: Herniation of small bowel through a mesenteric or peritoneal defect can twist the mesentery, creating a whirlpool appearance and causing intermittent or acute small-bowel obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Swirling configuration of mesenteric vessels
Clustered/twisted small-bowel mesentery that can be seen with internal hernia
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of abdominal surgery or gastric bypass is provided
No definite closed-loop bowel obstruction, bowel dilatation, or bowel wall ischemia is described
No clinical obstructive symptoms were provided

data.description: A benign congenital nonparasitic splenic cyst, often large and solitary, with internal echoes from proteinaceous or hemorrhagic material.
symptoms_in_common: Large well-circumscribed cystic lesion within the spleen
Relatively homogeneous low-level internal echoes within the cyst
Apparent compression/displacement of surrounding splenic parenchyma

data.description: A nonparasitic splenic cyst, commonly occurring after prior trauma, hemorrhage, or infection; it may contain debris, septations, calcification, or internal echoes.
symptoms_in_common: Large solitary splenic cystic lesion
Internal echogenic debris or low-level echoes
Rounded, encapsulated appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of splenic trauma, prior hemorrhage, or infection was provided
Wall calcification is not clearly demonstrated

data.description: A parasitic cyst caused by Echinococcus infection that can involve the spleen and may appear as a large cyst with internal debris, daughter cysts, or detached membranes.
symptoms_in_common: Large cystic lesion in the spleen
Internal echoes that could represent hydatid sand or debris
symptoms_not_in_common: Daughter cysts are not clearly visible
Detached internal membranes are not clearly visible
No exposure history, eosinophilia, or endemic-area history was provided

data.description: A localized infection within the spleen that may form a complex fluid collection with internal debris, septations, and occasionally gas.
symptoms_in_common: Complex cystic splenic lesion
Internal low-level echoes compatible with purulent debris
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic infectious symptoms were provided
No irregular thick wall, gas, or multiple abscesses are clearly visible
The lesion appears relatively well circumscribed and homogeneous

data.description: A benign congenital malformation of splenic lymphatic vessels that may present as one or more cystic lesions, often multiloculated with thin septations.
symptoms_in_common: Cystic lesion involving the spleen
Well-defined lesion with fluid-like internal characteristics
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears predominantly solitary rather than multicystic
Thin internal septations are not clearly demonstrated
No multiple peripheral splenic cysts are evident

data.description: A contiguous-gene deletion syndrome caused by a deletion of chromosome 11p11.2, typically involving EXT2, ALX4, and PHF21A. It is characterized by multiple osteochondromas/exostoses, enlarged parietal foramina, craniofacial abnormalities, and frequently developmental delay.
symptoms_in_common: Chromosome 11p11.2 microdeletion involving EXT2, ALX4, and PHF21A
Large bilateral parietal skull defects/enlarged parietal foramina
Multiple bony exostosis-like lesions around the elbow and pelvis
Skeletal abnormalities involving the upper and lower extremities

data.description: An autosomal dominant skeletal disorder, most often due to pathogenic variants or deletions involving EXT1 or EXT2, causing multiple cartilage-capped bony outgrowths near metaphyses of long bones.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bony exostosis-like lesions
Lesions near metaphyseal regions of long bones
Possible EXT2 involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Large bilateral parietal foramina/skull defects
Deletion involving ALX4 and PHF21A in addition to EXT2
Cranial ossification abnormality

data.description: A skull ossification disorder caused most commonly by pathogenic variants involving ALX4 or MSX2, producing persistent enlarged openings in the parietal bones near the sagittal suture.
symptoms_in_common: Large bilateral parietal skull defects
Persistent enlarged parietal foramina
ALX4 involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple bony exostosis-like lesions of the limbs and pelvis
EXT2 deletion
PHF21A deletion

data.description: A skeletal dysplasia usually caused by RUNX2 pathogenic variants, characterized by delayed closure of cranial sutures and fontanelles, clavicular hypoplasia, dental abnormalities, and delayed ossification.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent skull ossification defects
Delayed or abnormal cranial bone formation
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple osteochondroma-like exostoses
Chromosome 11p11.2 deletion involving EXT2, ALX4, and PHF21A
Localized enlarged parietal foramina as the dominant skull finding
No clavicular hypoplasia is shown

data.description: A severe, highly contagious infestation with Sarcoptes scabiei mites, often causing extensive crusting, hyperkeratosis, erosions, and numerous mites in the superficial epidermis.
symptoms_in_common: Extensive erythematous crusted and ulcerated scalp lesions
Multiple inflamed erosive plaques on the trunk
Visible mites within the stratum corneum on histology
Dermal inflammatory infiltrate
Skin ulceration and excoriation
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear thick widespread hyperkeratotic scaling is visible
Typical scabies distribution such as finger webs, wrists, genital area, and burrows is not shown
Pruritus is not reported

data.description: A pruritic skin infestation caused by Sarcoptes scabiei, usually producing papules, burrows, excoriations, and eczematous lesions; mites can be identified in the stratum corneum.
symptoms_in_common: Mites identified in the superficial epidermis/stratum corneum
Inflammatory skin lesions
Erosions and excoriation-like ulcerated areas
Erythematous plaques on the trunk
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion burden appears much more extensive and ulcerative than typical classic scabies
Scalp involvement is uncommon in most immunocompetent adults with classic scabies
Classic burrows and typical hand/wrist involvement are not shown
Pruritus, especially nocturnal itching, is not reported

data.description: Infestation by body lice that causes severe itching and excoriated papules or eczematous skin lesions, typically affecting the trunk and areas in contact with clothing seams.
symptoms_in_common: Inflamed erosive lesions on the trunk
Excoriated and ulcerated skin lesions
Possible secondary inflammatory changes
symptoms_not_in_common: The organism shown histologically is a mite in the stratum corneum rather than a louse on hair or clothing
Marked scalp crusting is not typical of body lice
No itching is reported
No lice eggs/nits on clothing or hairs are described

data.diagnosis: Impetiginized dermatitis or secondary bacterial skin infection
data.description: A bacterial superinfection, commonly due to Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, occurring in disrupted skin and producing crusting, erosions, ulceration, and inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Crusted scalp lesions
Erosions and ulceration
Erythema and dermal inflammation
Multiple inflamed lesions on the trunk
symptoms_not_in_common: Mites in the stratum corneum are not explained by bacterial infection alone
No purulent drainage, honey-colored crusting, fever, or systemic illness is reported
The pattern suggests a primary parasitic infestation rather than isolated bacterial infection

data.description: An immune-complex-mediated glomerular disease characterized by mesangial proliferation, lobular accentuation of the glomerulus, and thickening or duplication of capillary walls.
symptoms_in_common: Renal biopsy appearance suggests lobular glomerular hypercellularity and mesangial expansion
Possible capillary-wall remodeling consistent with a proliferative glomerulonephritis
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, urinalysis findings, kidney-function values, or complement levels were provided

data.description: Chronic diabetic kidney disease causing mesangial matrix expansion, glomerular basement-membrane thickening, and sometimes nodular Kimmelstiel-Wilson lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Renal biopsy image may show nodular mesangial expansion and glomerulosclerosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of diabetes mellitus was provided
No proteinuria, edema, hypertension, or progressive renal impairment was reported

data.diagnosis: Lupus nephritis, proliferative form (class III or IV)
data.description: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis caused by systemic lupus erythematosus, often producing marked mesangial and endocapillary proliferation with capillary-wall immune deposits.
symptoms_in_common: Glomerular hypercellularity and proliferative inflammatory appearance on the renal biopsy image
symptoms_not_in_common: No systemic lupus symptoms such as rash, arthritis, photosensitivity, serositis, or cytopenias were provided
No hematuria, proteinuria, renal dysfunction, or autoimmune serology results were reported

data.description: An immune-complex glomerular disease with predominantly mesangial IgA deposition, often causing mesangial proliferation and variable glomerular scarring.
symptoms_in_common: Mesangial proliferation in the glomerular biopsy image could be compatible with IgA nephropathy
symptoms_not_in_common: No episodic visible hematuria or microscopic hematuria was reported
No recent upper-respiratory infection, purpura, abdominal pain, or joint symptoms were provided

data.description: An immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disease causing bile-duct wall thickening and strictures, characterized by dense lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with increased IgG4-positive plasma cells. It may occur with or without autoimmune pancreatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging evidence of biliary ductal narrowing/stricture near the hepatic hilum
Biliary tree abnormality on MRCP
Dense lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory infiltrate on histology
Numerous IgG4-positive plasma cells on immunohistochemical staining
Inflammatory lesion that can mimic hilar cholangiocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear diffuse pancreatic enlargement or classic imaging appearance of autoimmune pancreatitis is shown
No clinical jaundice, pruritus, abdominal pain, fever, or elevated serum IgG4 level is provided

data.diagnosis: Autoimmune pancreatitis type 1 with associated IgG4-related cholangitis
data.description: Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis is the pancreatic manifestation of IgG4-related disease and can cause pancreatic inflammation, pancreatic enlargement, and associated stricturing of the bile ducts.
symptoms_in_common: Biliary stricture involving the extrahepatic or hilar biliary system
IgG4-rich plasma-cell infiltration in tissue
Lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory histology
Potential involvement of the pancreas and biliary tract in the same systemic immune-mediated process
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite sausage-shaped pancreatic enlargement is demonstrated
No pancreatic duct narrowing or irregularity is clearly described
The dominant lesion appears biliary/hilar rather than pancreatic
No symptoms of pancreatitis or pancreatic exocrine dysfunction are provided

data.description: A malignant tumor arising from the bile-duct epithelium at the hepatic hilum, typically producing obstruction of the right and left hepatic ducts and upstream biliary dilatation.
symptoms_in_common: Hilar biliary narrowing/obstruction on CT and MRCP
Infiltrative-appearing lesion at the porta hepatis
Appearance that may resemble a malignant biliary stricture
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology shows prominent lymphoplasmacytic inflammation rather than malignant atypical glandular cells
Abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells favor IgG4-related disease rather than cholangiocarcinoma
No definite mass-forming malignant lesion, metastases, or vascular invasion is shown
No clinical progressive painless jaundice, weight loss, or constitutional symptoms are provided
